moratorium. although recognising the serious nature of the crimes involved, we thought it was useful, because it always is, to reiterate the eu’s opposition to the use of the death penalty in all circumstances, without exception. the use of the death penalty represents an unacceptable denial of human dignity and integrity and, contrary to what some people argue, experience worldwide has demonstrated that it also fails to act as a deterrent to crime. in addition, it makes any miscarriage of justice – and those can happen in any legal system – irreversible. we look forward to continuing to engage with you and we will continue to do our utmost to ensure that this issue will be raised with the relevant authorities in bahrain and kuwait, as in any other country which applies the death penalty – because, of course, there are still many. we are aware that the fact of the death penalty is recognised in the legal systems of these countries but we know that authorities in other countries in similar situations have developed a pragmatic approach and have started to apply a moratorium. that is what we constantly encourage countries such as bahrain and kuwait to do. we will continue also, through the work with like-minded partners, with civil society and in various multilateral forums, to promote a global moratorium on the death penalty. we will be looking forward to working with you on this.
author. mr president, commissioner, twenty years of the guatemala peace accords: a long way to go, but still a long way to go. as long as there is a single human rights defender victim, we cannot be satisfied wholly the opposite neither in guatemala nor anywhere else. but with the same yardstick: we cannot look at some governments while we stop looking at others that keep political prisoners - and today is my memory for leopoldo lópez on his third anniversary of imprisonment. the resolution we are presenting is above all balanced. we appreciate the steps taken by the government - which are many - and encourage them to continue in this struggle, but we also show our concern for a situation of violence that has not been eradicated. we call for the involvement of the institutions, including the european union, in all areas, and we call for redoubling efforts against any kind of violence, pressure or intimidation: zero impunity. it is a clear commitment to freedom, democracy and respect for human rights in guatemala and anywhere in the world. human rights are universal and have no nationality.
author. mr president, madam commissioner, just a year ago i travelled to guatemala as vice-chair of the subcommittee on human rights and there i witnessed the extreme violence and insecurity suffered by human rights defenders, journalists, judges, indigenous leaders doubly if they are women, but i also witnessed the admirable work that the international commission against impunity is doing, and also the deep sense of justice of the guatemalan people. today, in february 2017, guatemala is in the midst of constitutional reform and has a historic opportunity to provide a legal framework and guarantee for the independence of the judiciary, the fight against impunity, the right of indigenous peoples to prior consultation, the establishment of a mechanism to protect human rights defenders, and the full application of the united nations guiding principles on business and human rights. we as the european union will be supporting and monitoring this process. well, except for the colleagues from united left, who say they defend the people, but we don't know which one. certainly not the one in guatemala.
mr president; sebastián alonso juan, human rights defender shot dead while participating in a demonstration against a mega hydroelectric project in huehuetenango; laura leonor vázquez, activist opposing the mining megaproject known as the san rafael mine, also shot dead. so, up to a macabre figure of sixteen female defenders killed and more than two hundred and fifty attacks last year in guatemala. what do all these people who suffer these attacks have in common? well, something that this parliament and mrs becerra too refuse to accept: they are human rights defenders, social leaders who oppose and fight against megaprojects by multinationals that condemn them to choose between emigrating or being exploited. we are talking about hydroelectric projects such as pojón ii and renace, mining projects such as fénix or oil projects such as the one carried out by the french company perenco in el petén, all of which are megaprojects of european transnational companies. it should be noted that the european union has a responsibility for these human rights violations linked to the activities of these transnational corporations in these countries, thanks to the european union's free trade agreements.
author. mr president, we welcome the drafting of this resolution. the truth is that the situation has gotten worse in terms of violence and impunity. in the last year we have had many deaths and many attacks on human rights defenders, environmental activists, even people like the director of the international commission against impunity, who has also been the victim of attacks on his person, which i think is a very relevant resolution. i also think it is necessary to say that, beyond the declarative, we must be able to see what the european union can do to change this climate of impunity, and there are some things that i think are important. first: support for the office of the prosecutor general and all its efforts against impunity. we expect the delegation and the institutions of the european union to support it. secondly, the whole mechanism has been put in place to implement the judgment of the inter-american court of human rights to protect the defenders. that's something you have to support to the end, it's very important. thirdly, in the reform of the constitutional judicial system, we have news that the guatemalan parliament may be able to water down the reform. it is very important that this reform be adopted in its entirety and we therefore also want to ask the european institutions and the delegation to insist on this line.
on behalf of the s&d group. this is a resolution which contains three major sections, ladies and gentlemen. on the one hand, a call for solidarity with a suffering people, a people as a whole who are suffering a horrible situation. but above all, it is an embrace for those who defend human rights and freedoms, for the ngos, for the human rights defenders, who are the victims of this horrible situation in guatemala. it is also a condemnation of organized crime, of drug crime, which is largely responsible for the problems suffered by the guatemalan people. it is also a demand that the government of guatemala make progress in defending human rights and protecting human rights defenders. it is also a call to the government of guatemala to ensure the independence of the judiciary and the thorough investigation of criminals and, above all, it is a call to the government of guatemala to continue fighting crime and corruption in that state. and finally, it is a call for the european union to help guatemala. not to restrict aid, but to help him fight what he's suffering.
president of the commission. – mr president, honourable members of this house, ladies and gentlemen, later this month in rome, 27 of our member states will stand shoulder to shoulder in peace, solidarity and friendship to mark the 60th anniversary of the treaties of rome, and i would like to see the president of parliament associated with these ceremonies. however, this will not simply be a birthday celebration. it should also be the birth moment of the european union of 27, and as we turn the page and commence a new chapter in our history, it is time we sought new answers to a question as old as our union is young: quo vadis europa at 27? europe’s founding fathers were visionaries. altiero spinelli and ernesto rossi, imprisoned by a fascist regime, dared to dream of a place where allies and adversaries would unite. unable to speak freely, they penned the manifesto for a free and united europe, which had to be circulated secretly in rome among the italian resistance movement in 1943. in writing this manifesto, this new chapter, spinelli and rossi decided not to cling to the darkness surrounding them in their ventotene prison cells. they stretched out their arms to the light instead. they dreamed of a better future and paved the way towards it. sixty years later, this should be an inspiration for us. with nothing to dim our voices, would we be forgiven for not speaking up? in 60 years’ time, what will our grandchildren say of our legacy? i want them to be proud, as spinelli and rossi would probably have been today. now is our time to be pioneers and to carve out a vision so that we may work hand in hand, united at 27, towards our future. sehr verehrter herr präsident, meine damen und herren, liebe kollegen! jeden tag ändert sich die welt um uns herum. die änderungen und veränderungen sind rasant. globalisierung, terrorismus, migration, die auswirkungen neuer technologien auf gesellschaft und arbeitsplätze verändern den alltag der europäer tiefgreifend. umstände, verhältnisse, zusammenhänge wechseln nicht jährlich, monatlich oder wöchentlich, sie wechseln täglich – so sehr und so schnell, dass wir manchmal außer atem kommen. vor uns liegen große herausforderungen und hohe hürden. sie sind groß und hoch, aber mitnichten unüberwindbar. entweder werden wir von solchen entwicklungen überholt, niedergewalzt, oder wir lassen uns auf sie ein, gestalten sie und ergreifen die neuen chancen, die sie mit sich bringen. europa darf nicht müde werden. europa muss hellwach sein und chancen und möglichkeiten aktiv, manchmal auch proaktiv, nutzen. wie es mein freund frank-walter steinmeier gesagt hat: wenn wir anderen mut machen wollen, brauchen wir selbst welchen. die zukunft europas darf nicht zur geisel von wahlperioden, parteipolitik oder kurzfristig innenpolitisch aufbereiteten erfolgsmeldungen werden. der brexit, so bedauerlich und schmerzhaft er auch sein mag, wird die europäische union auf ihrem marsch in die zukunft nicht stoppen können – wir machen weiter, wir müssen weitermachen! wohin gehst du, europa? quo vadis, europa? wohin steuert das europa der 27? es gibt eigentlich keinen besseren zeitpunkt und auch keinen anderen zeitpunkt als jetzt, um diese zugegebenermaßen schwierige debatte zu führen. alle überlegungen und debatten darüber, welchen weg wir einschlagen, müssen eine wesentliche aufgabe im blick haben, und die lösung dieser aufgabe muss unser aller handeln bestimmen. seien wir ehrlich: viel zu lange war das, was die menschen von europa erwarteten, zu weit entfernt von dem, was europa bieten und leisten konnte. unsere aufgabe wird es sein, deutlich zu machen, was europa kann und was europa nicht kann. nehmen wir zum beispiel die bekämpfung der arbeitslosigkeit und im besonderen der jugendarbeitslosigkeit. wir treffen uns gipfel um gipfel und versprechen die arbeitslosenzahlen, im speziellen die jugendarbeitslosigkeit, abzusenken. dabei liegt dies weit außerhalb der alleinigen möglichkeiten europas. auf europäischer ebene können wir keine wunder vollbringen, wenn die nationalen maßnahmen zu kurz greifen. wir können ausbildungsprogramme finanzieren, investitionen stimulieren – letzteres übrigens nicht ohne erfolg – doch das führt nicht automatisch und per se zu einem systematischen rückgang der arbeitslosigkeit. der eu-haushalt steuert lediglich 0,3 % zu den europäischen sozialhaushalten bei – 0,3 %! die mitgliedstaaten bringen 99,7 % auf. zu behaupten, europa stünde alleine in der verantwortung, wenn es um die bekämpfung der arbeitslosigkeit geht, ist schlicht falsch. dann sollen wir auch nicht so tun, als könne alleine europa das problem lösen. wir und die mitgliedsstaaten sollten dies endlich zugeben. wir sollten menschen nicht glauben machen, dass wir die sonne und den mond herbeizaubern können, wenn wir höchstens ein teleskop liefern können. wir sollten aufhören, absichten anzukündigen und sollten uns stattdessen stärker auf die bereiche konzentrieren, in denen wir handfeste ergebnisse liefern können. der ausgangspunkt für das weißbuch der kommission, das ich ihnen heute vorlege, ist folgender: es ist an der zeit – ich wiederhole mich –, dass wir klarstellen, was europa leisten kann und was nicht. viel zu oft wird die debatte über europas zukunft auf mehr oder weniger europa verkürzt. dieser ansatz führt aber in die irre, wie alle übertrieben vereinfachungen in die irre führen. im weißbuch stellen wir verschiedene wege für die zukunft der eu-27 vor: fünf szenarien für die europäische union der 27, wenngleich es in der wirklichkeit mehr möglichkeiten geben kann. nicht alle szenarien finden die spontane zustimmung der kommission, aber alle fünf szenarien sind im gespräch, ergo müssen wir uns mit ihnen beschäftigen. wir müssen darlegen, zu welchen folgen jedes einzelne dieser szenarien führen kann. schauen wir uns ein erstes szenario an, das auf eine fortsetzung der bisherigen politik abstellt. als diese kommission antrat, habe ich diesem haus versprochen, die dinge anders anzugehen, um das vertrauen der menschen wiederzuerlangen, und in weiten teilen gelingt uns das hoffentlich auch. die kommission hat bereits große fortschritte dabei erzielt, den althergebrachten reflex zu brechen, jeden aspekt im alltag der menschen regulieren zu wollen und uns in alles einzumischen. die menschen wollen nicht, dass wir vorschriften für toilettenspülungen oder für die höhe von kinderschaukeln erlassen. wir haben hunderte von vorschlägen zurückgezogen und schlagen anstatt 130 initiativen pro jahr, wie in früheren jahren üblich, lediglich 23 neue initiativen pro jahr vor. wir konzentrieren uns auf die großen dinge, die für den menschen wirklich wichtig sind. und trotzdem wird die kommission in allen hauptstädten, in fast allen nationalen parlamenten, manchmal auch hier, in fast der gesamten presse der überregulierung bezichtigt. dieses permanente brüssel-bashing macht keinen sinn, weil dieses brüssel-bashing seit dem amtsantritt dieser kommission keine grundlage hat. es täte uns allen im übrigen gut, wenn wir mit diesem brüssel-bashing, diesem european-union-bashing aufhörten. dies ist sehr oft ein ersatz für nationale versäumnisse. wir können so weitermachen, all unsere energie darauf zu lenken, ergebnisse in wichtigen bereichen zu erzielen und unsere positive agenda, die die zustimmung dieses hauses gefunden hat, voranzubringen. vollendung des binnenmarktes, des digitalen binnenmarktes, der energieunion, der kapitalmarktunion und der verteidigungsunion. das tun wir auch. und das werden wir tun. doch die frage muss erlaubt sein, ob das ausreichend ist. wir könnten auch den entgegengesetzten weg einschlagen und uns als europäische union der 27 ausschließlich auf den binnenmarkt beschränken: szenario 2. falls sich die mitgliedsstaaten in immer mehr politikbereichen nicht auf eine gemeinsame haltung verständigen können, falls immer mehr regierungen die kommission zu einem simplen binnenmarktverwalter degradieren möchten, wäre dies womöglich die einzige gangbare lösung. unsere lösung, meine lösung ist das nicht. die europäische union ist mehr als eine mehr oder weniger gehobene freihandelszone. europa ist mehr als markt, waren und geld. der binnenmarkt und der euro sind keine ziele an sich. sie haben dem menschen und den menschen zu dienen. trotzdem gibt es regierungen, die die rolle der europäischen union und ergo der kommission zurückdrängen möchten auf die binnenmarktverwaltung. ich bin strikt dagegen! dann gibt es eine dritte option, ein drittes szenario. müssen alle mitgliedsstaaten der europäischen union immer im gleichen tempo voranschreiten? wenn wir im kreise der 27 keine einigung erzielen können, weder was ziele noch die wege dahin betrifft, dann sollte es denjenigen, die in verschiedenen bereichen vorankommen wollen, erlaubt sein, weitere fortschritte dort zu machen, wo sie ihnen notwendig erscheinen. gleichzeitig müssen die anderen, die nicht am start dabei sein können oder nicht am start dabei sein wollen, die möglichkeit haben, sich absichten und taten der erststartenden später anzuschließen. doch wie würde sich ein solches system auswirken? für eine kleine anzahl von ländern könnte dieser ansatz große fortschritte mit sich bringen. für länder, die in einem derartigen rahmen etwa sämtliche informationen in der terrorismusbekämpfung austauschen, ein wirkliches europäisches asylsystem einrichten und verteidigungskapazitäten zusammenlegen möchten, wäre dies ohne jeden zweifel ein gangbarer weg. es könnte jedoch auch ein kompliziertes system konzentrischer kreise entstehen, in dem viele länder außerhalb des orbits zentraler politischer strategien kreisen würden. dadurch wäre europa noch schwerer verständlich, als es ohnehin schon ist. wie erklärte man beispielsweise den menschen, dass europa für die harmonisierung von frequenzen zuständig ist, auf denen autonom fahrende fahrzeuge bei einem unfall den rettungsdienst anrufen können, allerdings nur in den ländern x, y und z, und daher bekämen sie keine hilfe, wenn sie im land a unterwegs sind. die schwierigkeiten dieses ansatzes sehen wir bereits heute, wenn wir versuchen zu erklären, dass europa teilweise für die überwachung der schengen-außengrenzen zuständig ist, aber eben nur teilweise. und trotzdem: die vorstellung, dass einige mitgliedstaaten in teilbereichen voranschreiten und denen die bahn brechen, die sich erst später anschließen möchten, darf nicht ohne weiteres ad acta gelegt werden. diese form der avantgarde zielt nicht auf exklusion, sondern auf spätere inklusion. ich kann ehrlich gesagt dieser vorgehensweise einiges abgewinnen. ziel muss es bleiben, zu 27 voranzumarschieren. wenn sich dies aber als unmöglich erwiese, muss man der koalition der integrationswilligen die erlaubnis zum weiterfahren geben. europäische erfolge waren fast immer das werk vorauseilender pioniere. siehe schengen, siehe euro. (beifall) es gibt aber noch eine vierte möglichkeit: die eu-27 könnte gemeinsam beschließen, in einer etwas kleineren anzahl von bereichen vereint mehr zu tun. also in bereichen, in denen unsere europäischen maßnahmen einen echten mehrwert erzielen würden und in denen die menschen zu recht mehr von uns erwarten: szenario nummer 4. dies würde letztlich bedeuten, dass wir nach dem prinzip „weniger ist mehr“ verfahren. beispiele für bereiche, in denen die bürger mehr von uns erwarten, sind die sicherheitspolitik und das sogenannte dieselgate. eine echte europäische agentur für terrorismusbekämpfung, die informationen über grenzen hinweg austauscht und verdächtige systematisch beobachtet, könnte – davon bin ich überzeugt – einen greifbaren mehrwert für unser aller sicherheit bieten. genauso müssen sich europäische verbraucher, die durch technische manipulationen von automobilherstellern in die irre geführt werden, auf eine eu-agentur verlassen können, die sanktionen gegen täuschungsunternehmen durchsetzen kann und dafür sorgt, dass diese auch schadensersatz – und zwar überall – leisten müssen. anstatt die menschen dadurch zu enttäuschen, dass wir scharf formulierte schreiben versenden, in denen wir die mitgliedstaaten zum handeln auffordern, müssen wir sicherstellen, dass diesen aufforderungen auch folge geleistet werden kann. schließlich – szenario 5 – könnten die mitgliedstaaten auch beschließen, mehr befugnisse und ressourcen zu teilen und mehr entscheidungen gemeinsam zu treffen. sie könnten so vollgas geben, das neu geordnete gemeinsame in die zukunft hinein gestalten und die leadership der europäischen union sicherstellen. klimaschutz: hier muss europa weiterhin eine vorreiterrolle spielen, egal was jenseits des atlantiks ins haus steht. nachhaltige entwicklung: eine europäische daueraufgabe. verteidigung: hier müssen weitere eigenständige beiträge europas in aufstellung gebracht werden. toutes ces perspectives, toutes ces esquisses, tous ces projets théoriquement possibles sont des choix qui s’offrent à nous. tout en ayant récusé l’idée qu’il faudrait réduire l’union européenne à l’état de zone de libre-échange, ce qui n’est pas mon concept et qui ne correspond pas aux ambitions de l’europe, je ne vais pas vous dire ma préférence absolue aujourd’hui parce que, en fin de compte, ce n’est pas à moi seul – et je le regrette – ni à la commission de faire ces choix «in splendid isolation». je n’ai pas voulu présenter les vues définitives de la commission. je ne procède pas, alors que c’est devenu la mode, par «exécutive audace». la parole sera à votre parlement, aux parlements nationaux, aux gouvernements, à la société civile, bref, aux citoyens. contrairement à ce qui, jadis, fut la règle, la commission ne prescrit pas, ne dicte pas, n’instruit pas. elle veut être à l’écoute avant de se prononcer définitivement. pas de diktat – cela ne correspond pas à mon tempérament – mais de l’écoute. je ne suis pas un dictateur, mais j’aime dire les choses comme je les vois. j’aimerais annoncer la couleur, ma conception de l’union européenne dès aujourd’hui, et je mesure la déception de ceux qui auraient voulu que je le fasse. mais nous préférons écouter avant de dire. à ceux qui voudraient qu’avant le débat, la commission dise ce qu’elle voudrait être, je dirai qu’il ne faut pas confondre leadership et diktat. contrairement à ce qui a été fait jusqu’à présent, nous voulons d’abord écouter avant de nous prononcer. cela peut conduire – je l’ai lu – à des déceptions majeures, mais c’est une méthode qui fait honneur à la démocratie non seulement représentative mais aussi entière. parler d’institutions, de révision des traités, de procédures institutionnelles – débat qui agite ceux qui sont installés dans le confort de la bulle bruxelloise, qu’il faudra, à tout prix, que nous quittions tous ensemble – ne m’intéresse pas pour l’instant. d’ailleurs, un tel discours n’intéresserait pas les citoyens. vous, qui faites des réunions dans tous vos pays, vous a-t-on jamais posé une question sur l’équilibre des pouvoirs entre le conseil, la commission et le parlement? jamais! jamais je n’ai eu à répondre à une telle question! c’est donc un débat typiquement bruxellois qui, mis à part ceux qui sont installés dans le confort de la bulle bruxelloise, n’intéresse personne. il ne faudrait donc pas conduire ce débat. viendra, j’en suis certain, le jour où les traités devront être adaptés à une volonté collective, mais à une volonté collective à naître. car elle n’existe pas aujourd’hui. pour pouvoir donner corps à cette volonté collective, il nous faut un véritable débat, un débat honnête sur l’europe et sur ce que les citoyens attendent de l’union européenne. cette conversation vertueuse ne doit pas avoir lieu seulement à rome ou encore à l’occasion de nos nombreux sommets ou de nos nombreux débats ici même. elle doit avoir lieu dans les villes et les régions, partout en europe. c’est avec vous, mesdames et messieurs les députés, et avec les états membres que nous tiendrons une série de débats sur l’avenir de l’europe. chaque voix, même minuscule, à peine audible même, doit être entendue. les citoyens nous diront ce qu’ils attendent de l’union européenne. ils exprimeront vraisemblablement leurs doutes, leurs interrogations, mais aussi leurs espoirs. à nous d’y répondre. le livre blanc, que je vous invite à lire, y compris son introduction et l’échange des arguments pour et contre, nous aidera à formuler les bonnes réponses. au cours des prochains mois, la commission apportera de nouvelles contributions à ce large débat avec une série de documents de réflexion et de propositions plus précises portant sur les grands enjeux dont demain sera fait. nous présenterons nos idées sur le renforcement de la dimension sociale, débat à mes yeux essentiel et auquel j’apporte toute mon attention. ceux qui applaudissent, lorsqu’on parle d’europe sociale, ne font pas la majorité dans cette salle. honte à vous! parce que l’europe sociale est un enjeu principal pour les décennies à venir. nous présenterons nos vues sur l’approfondissement de l’union économique et monétaire et, notamment, sur les mécanismes qui amélioreront la très nécessaire coordination des politiques économiques. nous présenterons nos vues sur la maîtrise de la mondialisation et nos réflexions sur l’avenir de la défense de l’europe et l’avenir des finances de l’union européenne. en matière de défense, il est évident que les états européens devront augmenter leur budget militaire, mais la stabilité planétaire n’est pas seulement fonction de l’ampleur des budgets militaires. la stabilité internationale, mondiale, planétaire est aussi fonction de la dimension des budgets d’aide au développement et du financement de la lutte contre le changement climatique. réduire les budgets de l’aide au développement, remettre en cause les engagements qui furent les nôtres et ceux des autres en matière de changement climatique – je parle de la cop 21 – nuira gravement à la stabilité intégrale. l’union européenne doit porter et continuer à porter ces messages. la stabilité, ce n’est pas seulement l’affaire des armées, c’est aussi l’affaire de ceux qui veulent aider ceux qui sont en retard à rejoindre ceux qui sont en avance. la stabilité, ce sont les dépenses militaires, mais pas exclusivement; c’est aussi l’aide au développement et la lutte contre le changement climatique. mesdames et messieurs, vous vous êtes déjà penchés sur toutes ces questions et nous nous réjouissons à l’idée de continuer à travailler avec vous et notamment avec les rapporteurs qui ont vu leurs rapports adoptés récemment. je prends rendez-vous avec vous en septembre, lors du discours sur l’état de l’union, où je développerai davantage ces idées, pas avant, mais après avoir écouté les uns et les autres. j’aimerais que le conseil européen donne en décembre ses orientations pour un processus qui atteindra son apogée lors des élections européennes en 2019. en 2019, nous avons rendez-vous avec le suffrage universel européen. ce sera d’abord un rendez-vous d’explications. explications entre les forces politiques, c’est-à-dire entre les familles politiques, qui devront dire comment elles voient l’europe de 2025 et au-delà. je voudrais que le processus démocratique engagé en 2014 connaisse son prolongement, c’est-à-dire qu’en 2019, les partis européens présentent au choix de l’électeur des têtes de liste, exigence qu’il faudra que nous respections pour que la démocratie européenne fonctionne et reste crédible. en 2019, nous ne pourrons pas renoncer à l’acquis que nous avons réalisé en 2014, ensemble. je salue d’ailleurs amicalement les candidats qui n’ont pas eu la chance que j’ai pu avoir. (jean-claude juncker réplique à m. verhofstadt qui disait hors micro: «la prochaine fois».) les citoyens européens doivent pouvoir décider qui sera le prochain président de la commission européenne. les citoyens doivent pouvoir faire leur choix, pas les officines gouvernementales. je ne serai pas candidat à un deuxième mandat, comme je l’ai dit dès le premier jour. (applaudissements venant de la droite de l’hémicycle.) (en réaction à ces applaudissements) j’avais pour intention de ne jamais décevoir l’extrême-droite, j’ai réussi. je ne serai pas candidat à un deuxième mandat, mais, croyez-moi, je ne suis ni fatigué ni à court d’idées, au contraire, et vous allez le voir. monsieur le président, l’europe s’est relevée des cendres de la seconde guerre mondiale pour réaliser l’impossible: mettre fin à cette éternelle tragédie européenne qui, en fait, nous obligeait – les peuples, leurs dirigeants – à choisir entre la guerre et la paix. dans le monde d’aujourd’hui, plus de quarante guerres et conflits militaires font rage, mais pas un seul ne se déroule sur le sol européen proprement dit. vu de plus loin et à partir d’autres continents, l’europe continue à rester une chose magnifique: avoir réuni tout un continent, avoir mis un terme à ce funeste décret d’après-guerre qui voulait que l’europe, à tout jamais, soit scindée en deux blocs, y avoir créé un espace de stabilité, de prospérité et d’égalité nous vaut l’admiration du monde entier. très souvent, j’ai l’impression que les autres nous admirent et que nous-mêmes, il nous arrive de nous détester. mais cette europe, celle que je décris, n’est pas un acquis, ni une évidence. l’europe a toujours été et reste aujourd’hui et pour toujours un choix délibéré, qu’il faut défendre contre vents et marées, contre l’assaut de ceux qui ne veulent pas comprendre le cours de l’histoire. les choix que nous faisons maintenant, aujourd’hui, demain, dans deux ans et d’ici 2025 doivent tenir compte de leurs implications, non seulement pour nous, mais surtout pour les générations à venir. parce que nous serons jugés, non pas sur ce qui nous a été légué, mais sur ce que nous laisserons en héritage. nos citoyens nous disent souvent que nous devons faire les choses différemment. oui, nous y sommes prêts, mais il ne faut pas vouloir tout changer. nous devrions essayer de mieux comprendre les contraintes et les chances d’une application correcte du principe de subsidiarité, qui ne doit pas devenir un ersatz pour la solidarité, laquelle doit, elle, rester le principe directeur de toutes nos actions européennes et nationales. très souvent, en écoutant ceux qui se font l’avocat du principe de subsidiarité, j’ai l’impression que, comme ils ne veulent pas parler de solidarité, ils préfèrent parler de subsidiarité. il s’agit de bien comprendre la signification exacte du concept de subsidiarité. monsieur le président, nous n’avons pas le droit d’être – comment dire – patriotes contre les autres. le patriotisme du xxie siècle se décline en deux dimensions: un patriotisme heureux, accepté et acceptable vers l’intérieur, et la solidarité, qui est le prolongement du patriotisme heureux vers l’extérieur. il y a des valeurs qui doivent continuer de nous unir: la paix, la démocratie, la solidarité, l’état de droit – qui doit être la règle qui sous-tend notre vivre-ensemble très souvent menacé –, la dignité et l’égalité de tous les êtres humains, ainsi que la liberté de la presse. regardez ce qui se passe en turquie où l’on emprisonne, sans raison aucune, des journalistes allemands parce qu’ils ont osé dire ce qu’il fallait dire! les valeurs, oui, ce qui inclut le refus du rejet de l’autre, de celui qui est différent de nous, mais qui n’est pas moins noble que nous-mêmes. nous ne pouvons pas accepter que les voix de ceux qui défendent ces valeurs, dont je voudrais qu’elles soient universelles, soient noyées dans le vacarme des slogans nationalistes qui font du patriotisme une arme contre les autres. le patriotisme n’est plus un patriotisme lorsqu’il se dirige contre les autres. l’europe, elle, doit rester une force mondiale positive. nos sociétés européennes sont bâties sur l’ouverture et nous devrions en être plus fiers. d’autres préfèrent se refermer sur eux-mêmes et tourner leur regard vers l’intérieur. le nombrilisme fait des progrès angoissants à travers la planète. mais une telle attitude n’est ni dans notre nature, ni d’ailleurs dans notre intérêt. la démocratie – la démocratie entière – est un produit européen et nous la défendrons partout et de toutes nos forces. alors, ayons le courage, la patience et la détermination qui sont nécessaires aux longs trajets et aux grandes ambitions. l’europe continue à être une grande ambition. une ambition qui a derrière elle et devant elle un long trajet. nous avons aujourd’hui le choix entre plusieurs chemins, certains plus pernicieux que d’autres, d’autres plus porteurs d’avenir que d’autres. monsieur le président, quel que soit le choix que nous ferons, la destinée de l’europe à vingt-sept est entre nos mains. entre nos mains, oui, mais elle est d’abord et avant tout une affaire de cœur et une affaire de valeurs, de valeurs qui donnent sa véritable dimension à la raison d’état européenne. je ne suis pas en train de citer un poème européen, je décris une nécessité continentale. the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, health systems are part of the social europe in which european citizens recognise and value each other; they are crucial to ensuring social cohesion and also productivity, which generate a healthy society. but they face challenges, like sustainability, because of the aging population, the increase in chronic disease, the emergence of new technologies. but today, we are mainly here because of the increase in pharmaceutical spending: 17% of all health spending 1.4% of the gdp of the european union. the high prices of medicines have put us, the developed countries, in a situation which we did not think we would ever face: hepatitis c - a disease with serious consequences, but which today, with a cure, has not yet been able to hope to eradicate, but we are giving priority, on the basis of guidelines, to its treatment, which is difficult to justify from an ethical point of view. but cancer also threatens 24 million new cases by 2030, a 68 percent increase from 2012. but this is not a question of ethics, it is also a question of rights. article 35 of the charter of fundamental rights protects the right to health. the medicinal product as such cannot be considered a consumer good, but must be specially regulated so that the patient is at the centre of access to it. but, in addition to prices and sustainability, we have the problems of shortages, the lack of adaptation to needs due to lack of commercial interest - in aspects such as antimicrobial resistance - or the need to put incentives - as is the case with orphan drugs - problems in competition for generics to enter or lack of innovation with small modifications in many cases. the price of medicines is set by the industry on the basis of value, lacking other balances that guarantee access to citizenship. orphan drugs are increasing in numbers that make one think that the criteria are being applied incorrectly, because they generate a quick business, a quick return on investment. they are concerned, as i said, about the competitive litigation which is making it difficult for generics to enter the market. all of this seems to be leading or may be leading to a business model that makes it difficult for european citizens to access medicines. the member states, with confidential agreements, with co-payment, in short, with different measures, try to find a solution, but in the end what we have is a more fragmented and more unequal market. the commission sets up public incentives, but they also do not guarantee that return to society through a fair price or access. the balance of power is crucial to us and, to that end, the therapeutic value added is crucial and must be established by the commission and the member states in a coordinated manner. we need a legislative framework, commissioner, to ensure this, and we also need to look at other economic and social criteria, of course, to ensure this. we need to assess the real impact of intellectual property on the promotion of innovation and the quality of innovation and, ultimately, on access to medicines, the social purpose which really justifies this fundamental right as well. we need to evaluate the public incentives put in place and also ensure the return on investment is fair with a fair price and guaranteed access. we need a better framework to ensure competition and entry for generics and rational use of medicines. but, most especially, today i want to call for - and we cannot delay any longer - a plan to eradicate hepatitis c. it is immoral, it is unsustainable that today, when we have life-saving medicines, we are not able to coordinate sufficiently to eradicate this disease. in short, this report proposes these and other measures and actions, and i ask the commissioner to take this initiative and, before the end of the year, to present us with a legislative proposal. parliament joins the council, the un and the oecd. it is a popular cry that we must respond to this just demand.
i would like to conclude by congratulating the rapporteur on his announcements. he takes up the glove, shows his commitment, announces that he is going to launch or make a proposal on the evaluation of technologies, in particular medicines. i think that will provide an answer, which will be very important for what some groups have claimed here: the need to have an objective criterion so that we can set a fair price and avoid excesses in some cases, as has been shown here. i welcome your review of incentives to meet the effective objective for which they are mandated or your review of the impact of intellectual property. the report also calls for a review of the directive, for a strategy to combat antimicrobial resistance, a strategy against cancer, also for paediatric medicines, of course, to address the shortage of supplies in countries, especially in the east, and for greater coordination and transparency between member states. in short, it is a complex picture, but i believe that in the report, with the help of everyone, we have been able to collect it, and we have been able to point it out for exploration, to reach what we all here have seen and shared. we share, and i think there is a general consensus, the need to ensure the sustainability of health systems and to guarantee access to medicines for european citizens. i can only conclude by thanking all the alternative rapporteurs - and also the rapporteurs for the deve, juri and peti opinions - for their invaluable contribution and, of course, their capacity for dialogue, so that we can have this report, which has enjoyed a broad consensus in the committee and which i hope will have the same support tomorrow, so that we can support the initiatives that the commissioner is going to launch and, in the end, improve the quality of life of european citizens.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin by thanking all my colleagues on the committee on culture and education, who have worked with me in a spirit of cooperation and mutual understanding on this report on the implementation of the europe for citizens programme. the europe for citizens programme is the only one of the european commission's programmes aimed at promoting direct participation of citizens in the union and fostering dialogue between the institutions, civil society organisations and local authorities. that is why we have asked the committee on culture to increase the budget for the programme so that the objectives set can be achieved. firstly, it should be recalled that the budget agreed for this programme for the period 2014-2020 was significantly reduced by 14% compared to the previous period. in parliament and in the committee on culture and education we have been asking for an increase in the budget, to the tune of 500 million euro, in order to be able to adequately meet the project proposals that reach the evaluation agencies. moreover, if we compare it with the budget for the erasmus and creative europe programmes, which we have just discussed, it is clear that a greater financial effort is needed for this programme. secondly, we have asked the commission to develop a more innovative communication strategy. it is essential that this programme is better known in europe. unlike others, europe for citizens is not as popular and participation is very low among non-governmental organisations, foundations dealing with european citizenship issues, local authorities and networks of regions and cities that are its target groups. we need a more effective and accessible platform, which allows for a thorough knowledge of the funds available and a strengthening of relations with the contact points in the member states. we want all local organisations and administrations to be fully aware of the possibilities offered by this programme and for the participating countries which have not yet done so to designate a national contact point. thirdly, we believe that the european memory area of the europe for citizens programme should take account not only of europe's past and its memory, but also of its future. we want to convey a historical narrative that is not obsessed with differences, but tries to overcome them in a spirit of integration. we believe that this project will contribute to a more optimistic and integrated vision of europe, with a view to forging a common future. last but not least, the report states unequivocally that the next generation of the programme should be adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure, putting parliament on an equal footing with the council. i would like to stress that as the only institution of the union directly elected by the citizens, the european parliament must play its role as the union's co-legislator when it comes to approving a programme specifically designed to encourage the participation of citizens. in my report i therefore urge the commission to find a suitable legal basis for the next generation of the programme, which will allow the european parliament to be genuinely involved in the process of adopting and implementing this programme. that is why i ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to support the report as it was adopted in committee.

mr president, commissioner, the proposal the commission has put before us was frankly bad. it was a proposal which was not in accordance with the minamata convention or our own waste legislation. the commission proposed the less stringent option, which is the permanent storage of mercury in liquid form, without treatment and exclusively in salt mines. it was a proposal apparently tailored to the present situation, despite the fact that from these storage sites - and according to written replies from the commission - more than a thousand tonnes of mercury have been illegally transported to switzerland, the netherlands and greece, to be sold in third countries. fortunately, parliament has rectified this and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr eck, and all the alternative rapporteurs, especially mr dantin, for their attention to technical and environmental arguments. from now on, mercury will only be allowed to be stored temporarily on the surface. final storage must be carried out in surface or salt mines and, if surface, must be solidified and treated. the best technicians and experts in handling mercury are in my region, in the county of almadén, the largest mine in the world, and they believe that mercury should only be removed if there is a prior treatment of solidification. finally, madam commissioner, i would like to invite the commission to appear before the committee on the environment to explain the fraud that has occurred, as i have said before, in recent years and to give us reliable figures and tell us what has been done and whether there have been any sanctions. and also, tell us whether you are finally going to authorize the treatment of mercury in its reversion to mercury sulphide in switzerland, because in switzerland the european union has no power to control. commissioner, i am sorry to express myself in these terms, but i beg you to understand me. i'm from almadén. a region that was rich and prosperous thanks to mercury and that today is depressed and depopulated while seeing that far away they are getting rich with mercury that has come out of their mines and is being sold illegally.
the rapporteur. mr president, first of all i would like to thank all the rapporteurs who have been working with me on the report. it's been a pleasure, actually. i think we have done a good job of analysing the state of gender equality at the european union level. i would also like to thank - and i would like to mention it in particular - the european institute for gender equality, because without them, without their help, it would have been much more difficult to be able to produce this report - with all the analyses they do, the data they collect, the index they develop, which i think is extremely positive - from this point of view, i would also like to thank them. the report aims to send a very clear message, and that is that, judging from the data and the concrete analysis of certain indicators, we are stuck, if we do not take steps backwards, on gender equality at the level of the european union. and this is the first thing we have to recognize because this is not installed in the public debate, nor in the political debate. and i think it's important that we say that. if we take the indicator of the pension gap, it is not just that we are still at 40%, but that in half the member states the gap has widened. if you take the wage gap, we're at 16.2, which is basically the same level as we had in 2012; we've made practically no progress. in terms of political participation, progress in recent years has been only 6%. we're going very slowly, even in this house, where we've gone from a 30 to a 37. yes, there is progress, but it's very, very scarce. and then, the violence data. not only because of the cases we are seeing repeatedly in many of our member states, but also because of the data, and in this case the report refers to the study and the survey of the european agency for fundamental rights, based in vienna, which revealed that 33 per cent of women admitted to having been victims of some episode of violence in their lives, and 55 per cent admitted to having been victims of some episode of sexual harassment at some point in their lives. so i think we have to acknowledge that this data is not good. and the question we have asked ourselves and shared with the other speakers is how the institutions are responding to this question. and it's true -- and this is not just at the level of the european union, but also at the level of many member states -- that the equality agenda is pretty much blocked. we have had times when there was a lot of ambition in this area - even here, legislatively, and in many member states - and now this is no longer the case. and of course i have to refer to some of the things that are going on, particularly in the council. the commission withdrew the maternity leave directive because of the council's blockade - although we are obviously waiting for commissioner jourová to present to us, as she announced last time, on the 24th, the new package of measures, which we are obviously prepared to work on getting through - but we also have the directive on quotas in the blocked boards, and, in the area of violence, we are in the process of ratifying the istanbul convention, and one of the things the report calls for is that this be done as quickly and as swiftly as possible, and for all those member states which have not yet done so to do so as quickly as possible. but we also want to call for a specific instrument to combat gender-based violence at european union level, which we believe is absolutely essential. and of course, other calls we make are very important. as regards the directive on quotas in boards of directors, if we take the results in norway, for example, we see that the results are very effective, and i think it would be good if the council would unblock this dossier once and for all. the same is true, for example, of the wage gap. we have the announcement this week from the icelandic government that it's going to force all companies with more than 25 employees to explain how they ensure equal pay within the company. well, these are measures that i think we should also be replicating at the level of the european union. and the last thing i have to in writing. in the case of the opinion i was responsible for in the itre committee, the opinion on waste disposal, we would like to see the introduction of a waste management hierarchy to avoid incineration and disposal as much as possible. however, it is worrying that the management of this process falls massively on the private sector and that incineration continues to be promoted as an alternative to landfills (even with advantages for energy input to the grid) when in some regions its environmental impact may be higher. i would also like to stress that we have put forward proposals of great importance, such as the progressive closure of landfills, public consultation with municipalities and other stakeholders concerned, the recovery of closed landfills, the audit of existing landfills and greater control of waste. in spain (with four pending judgments on illegal landfills) landfills are unfortunately still used on a massive scale. impact assessments are avoided by expanding capacity, the levels of use of capacity are not controlled, etc. leading to environmental and public health emergencies which we hope the new directive will help to combat.
in writing. the member states set themselves the objective of identifying measures that the european commission will have to put in place in relation to the so-called 'circular economy'. the ultimate aim of the new european circular economy package is to promote the transition from a linear economy, where the maxim of 'use and throw away' is paramount, to a circular economy where waste is minimised and treated as a useful resource. in short, it is about making products reusable after they reach the end of their useful life. in this way, we will not only create value, but also influence climate change and the environment, and boost global competitiveness, sustainable economic growth and job creation. the generation of waste is a heterogeneous reality which makes it difficult to reuse it as a quality raw material, because there is no adequate separation and classification from the source. it is also well known that each member state separates differently, even between regions within the same state. we therefore hope that the new legislation will guarantee the quality of the waste generated and thus the quality of the raw materials so that they can be really reused.

member of the commission. – madam president, honourable members, i am very pleased to appear before the plenary here today to successfully conclude our work on the regulation on official controls. this is a very important piece of legislation. it is, as you know, the result of the joint and dedicated efforts of the parliament, the council and the commission. the outcome is, i believe, a credit to all three institutions. indeed, they all recognise the importance to provide member states’ authorities with effective and efficient enforcement tools to ensure the coherent application of european law. consumers and businesses should feel reassured that the control system across the eu is fit for purpose and safeguards the safety and quality of the entire agri-food chain. in particular, the new regulation will, first, introduce a more comprehensive approach to official controls along the entire agri-food chain by extending its scope to cover plant health and animal by-products. second, it requires member states to regularly perform controls to identify fraudulent practices and enable the establishment of new european union reference standards for the authenticity and integrity of the agri-food chain. third, re-enforce rules on financial penalties for fraudulent or deceptive practices by requiring that those penalties reflect the economic advantage either of the operators or a percentage of the operators’ turnover. fourth, introduce new provisions for the protection of whistle-blowers reporting on possible cases of non-compliance. fifth, strengthening the mechanism of administrative assistance and cooperation among member states in case of cross-border non-compliance. six, create a common framework of carrying out border controls on animals and goods entering the eu. and finally, seventh, increase the transparency of official control activities carried out by national authorities. the regulation is a major step forward to provide national enforcers with the powers and tools to effectively deliver on their control tasks. i therefore look forward with both hope and expectation to a broad agreement and endorsement of this file. our work will, of course, continue with the development of delegated acts and implementing acts and through the practical implementation of the new rules, once adopted.
on behalf of the ppe group madam president i'm not sure. i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs kadenbach, on her work and also thank all the alternative rapporteurs, the council and the commission for the spirit of collaboration we have had during the negotiation to reach this agreement. if i may, i would also like to make a special mention of our former colleague, mr schnellhardt, who was responsible for this report in my political group at the first reading. he very strongly defended the role of official veterinarians, which is one of the most debated issues. the regulation will continue to maintain the key role of veterinarians, but at the same time allow for some flexibility by being able to delegate some tasks. it will of course always allow the specificities of the member states to be taken into account in the interests of subsidiarity, and these delegations will also be very regulated, clearly specifying which tasks can be delegated and whether or not the veterinarian has the power to supervise, and clarifying who has the ultimate responsibility. another very important point, which parliament has fought for and achieved, is that checks are generally carried out without warning and on the basis of risk. this will enable the control bodies to manage resources according to those sectors which most need to be controlled. as i have said on several occasions, the european union has the best legislation on food safety, traceability, animal health and animal welfare, and we must monitor compliance with it. we don't need any more legislation. what is needed is more controls and an effective system of sanctions to deter those who break the law. i think we should welcome the fact that fraud is now part of the scope of the regulation. all risks will be taken into account, not just the health risks. recent scandals in the food chain made it clear that sanctions were not enough. from now on, the perpetrator of fraud will be sanctioned not only according to the economic benefit obtained but also according to the turnover of the company or person committing the fraud. the regulation we are about to adopt also clarifies the measures to be applied in respect of imported products, which also have to be controlled and have to be subject to the same rules as european products. cases such as xylella fastidiosa, which continues to affect our olive trees dramatically, or the black spot on citrus fruit are examples of the importance of controls on imported products. funding has also been a controversial issue. given the complexity of the issue, we have tried to strike a balance, because we need food security at the same time as we need to make sure certain controls are carried out. and to do that, they have to be funded. the agreement has maintained the status quo of the existing regulation, i.e. compulsory levies for the meat sector and imports, which will allow member states to have sufficient funds to control all sectors at risk. i would add that above all there will be a great deal of transparency with regard to the funding and the way in which the funding has been provided.
commissioner, three brief remarks on this debate: firstly, we ask that in developing this legislation specific rules be adopted so that home-made products and small-scale processing have their own legislation to allow their continuity and sale on local markets and short-distance sales. secondly, the strengthening of controls must prevent pests such as the solanivora tecia, known in galician as the guatemalan potato blight, from continuing to enter the territory of the european union and spreading through our countries. thirdly, we are calling for legislation to tackle the source of the biggest food scandals. i am referring to the logic of the industrial production mode. and i want to remind you that meat meal was legal and it caused one of the biggest scandals known in the european union. today's controls will not prevent the gmos or pesticide scandals of tomorrow.

because they will not always come from outside to defend us - that we must guarantee the permanence of our values and the security of our citizens. the report we are presenting today expresses the position of this parliament to move forward in building a europe of security and defence and reminds us that we cannot start the house by the roof. the treaty of lisbon is a coherent institutional framework and is sufficient to pave the way. there is no need for new treaties. the problem is, so far, we haven't used it. because - let us not be mistaken - the little progress that has been made in the common european defence to date depends only on the lack of political will on the part of the states and not on the lack of legal instruments. we therefore call on the states to participate in the mechanisms of permanent structured cooperation and in the creation of an integrated european force, as provided for in the protocol. we welcome the commission's announcement of the launch of the first joint planning military headquarters, which is also a demand of this report and which should serve as the embryo of the future headquarters of the european union for its military operations. this report makes it very clear - this is important - and allow states to launch projects that they could not do on their own, especially those that are not the largest. and it will improve coordination and information sharing, which are some of the most important tasks that we have to do. in this report we also call for the european defence agency to have full political, economic and operational backing. i therefore ask you to vote in favour of this report, so that it can serve as a road map for the european commission and also for the rome declaration next week, which has made security and defence one of its priorities. the european parliament must take the lead in the search for a common defence and security project. we cannot move forward unless all countries are genuinely committed to achieving it; there are no excuses. because there is no greater respect for national sovereignty, for the territorial integrity of each of our countries, than to be able to defend it jointly, each one contributing the best he has. the common european defence is already an urgent matter on which the future of the union also depends. no one's ever coming to defend us again. we'll have to defend ourselves from now on and for that, the first thing is to organize.

the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are discussing tonight, and voting on tomorrow, is about linking communication technologies with democracy. it may seem like a strange equation, but it's not. the idea behind the report is to establish the improvements that our democracy could achieve through communication technologies, on the understanding that our democracy is indeed suffering, particularly in recent years - i would say more specifically with the economic crisis - a setback; i do not know whether it is a discredit, but a certain distance from citizens towards public institutions. we are concerned about this, and the question is whether the networks and communication technologies could actually help us to improve this relationship, given that the gap, the distance between citizens and politics, has become ever wider, owing to the complexity of the issues raised by governance; to the economic crisis, which has transferred to certain economic institutions, outside of democracy itself, the power to decide on people's lives; and, in general, to the phenomena of political discrediting that parties and some representatives in some countries, for example, have been generating through corruption. this state of affairs worries us and the reflection that brought us to change was the idea that we had to take advantage of communication technologies to give it a meaning, i would not say new, but yes more positive to this relationship between citizenship and democracy. the report's balance sheet, of course, starts from the consideration that this is possible, that technologies are there to help us, not the other way around. and in that sense, we emphasize the importance that, for example, communication technologies could have, and already have in e-governance, in relation to what is the relationship between citizen and public administration, when we establish their fiscal relationship, when we access public services. there is a whole e-governance that has to serve to improve that relationship. there is an opportunity for e-participation to help citizens become more involved in the deliberation of democratic processes, in the consultations that governments can have with citizens about the impacts of certain measures, in evoting the ability to vote online, in political parties and their relationship with their affiliates, with their supporters and with their citizens. so there is a positive approach to the idea that technologies can help us enrich democracy and bring it closer to the citizens. but there is also a prudent look at these effects. it is not an alternative democracy, the report says. we cannot be so naive as to believe that we are going to invent a new democracy on the basis of direct democracy, since technologies, while facilitating that possibility, do not really replace the system of representative democracy. it's prudent, because the report warns of risks. there is a risk in digital access to participation platforms, which have to be equitable for everyone to have access; it's the risk of privacy, of securing the rights of individuals so that their rights are guaranteed. the whole of this situation calls for a report which has been approved by a majority of the whole house.

dynamics in various countries, so there is no single solution. tackling it requires action at many levels – at the international, national and local levels – and through joint efforts by different on behalf of the alde group. the regulation we are presenting today - and i would also like to thank mr kuhn, the rapporteur, for the effort he has made to bring about such a broad agreement - is vitally important for two reasons. firstly, because it will be essential to be able to determine the conditions for all member states to see their fishing capacity and because it provides guarantees so that the degree of respect for the capacity limits set out in the basic cfp regulation can be measured. it therefore provides legal certainty and clarity for all types of operations in the union relating to the exercise of the fishing profession. to this end, this regulation sets out a definition of all the parameters used to define and describe fishing vessels, such as length, beam, date of entry into service and engine power, which will allow these definitions to be applied to all european union rules on fishing. in making these definitions we have looked at the initiatives of the specialized international organizations and, of course, for specific aspects such as engine power, at the standards of the international organization for standardization (iso) which are usually applied to measures adopted in other sectors of activity. finally, these are definitions which are consistent with the common fisheries policy, and this will enable us to bring coherence to all the policies and all the legislation of this house.
the rapporteur. madam president, i would like to thank first of all the shadow rapporteurs for their contributions and also the teams that made this report possible. in rural areas there are different types of women with different professions and, like all women, they suffer the consequences of a patriarchal system which oppresses, discriminates and makes them unviable. despite progress in equality legislation, we see that there is still a long way to go. the fact is that existing laws are not fully applied or are implemented, often on a sexist basis. this was interfering with the advancement of our rights. i hope that this report on rural women will help to strengthen the struggle and to make progress in terms of full recognition of the rights of rural women. the challenges are important: in the professional field, in conciliation, in public services and in the fight against gender-based violence. the gender pay gap persists and unemployment affects women more. i shall refer in particular to the situation of women farmers. the policies of deregulation of production and markets, promoted by the cap, have led to precariousness and the loss of many jobs on farms and in the countryside. the failure to recognise shared ownership in family farms means that only 30% of female farmers in the european union are farm holders. all other women on this type of farm are deprived of the rights that come with owning it. we are talking, for example, about economic income and rights arising from the cap. these women also face difficulties in obtaining support under positive action measures to support women workers, as has already happened in many member states. the way in which the cap distributes aid, favouring large farms, also harms women who are usually the owners of smaller farms. for example, in 2013, on average, a farm managed by a woman is 8 hectares, compared to 20 hectares on farms managed by men, or 8 livestock units compared to 26 for men. but there is also the fact that many farmers are not considered as such because they do not contribute to agricultural social security. others, on the other hand, have few years of contribution when they reach retirement age, and this deepens the pension gap and brings higher levels of poverty to women. it is therefore essential to tackle this situation of discrimination and insecurity for women at its root if we are to maintain farms which are the fundamental economic basis for the development of a living rural environment. the report proposes that the member states and the commission should focus on shared ownership in family farms, in particular by drawing up laws to establish and implement it effectively where it already exists. the participation of women in all areas of decision-making, such as institutions, trade unions, cooperatives and also in negotiation processes must be guaranteed. public and quality services should target the rural environment, education, health, social services, transport or postal services. in conclusion, i would like to say that it is essential to equip rural areas with the tools to implement measures to prevent and eradicate gender-based violence and to ensure that support and counselling services are also provided for women affected by this violence.

madam president, this report on women and their role in rural areas is very important because we are calling on the european commission and the member states to take action to promote rural development, where women play an essential role, not only economically but also socially. many of our demands in the form of amendments, and also thanks to the work of my colleague lidia and mrs petir, are reflected in this report. for example, a high level of public services can be ensured in rural areas, because otherwise it will be impossible to establish population. we call for the right of women to farm ownership to be guaranteed, we also encourage gender-sensitive budgets and, finally, we recall the need to strengthen the means of combating gender-based violence in rural areas. in short, if we want gender equality and cohesion to be more than just principles written into the treaties, concrete public policies must be developed to ensure that the rural environment survives.
madam president, women produce more than half the world's food, but only a minority own their land: invisible work, difficult access to finance, the low representation of women in decision-making positions are a constant in the rural world. we greens believe that the current model of agriculture, which is industrial, globalised and intensive, is not only unsustainable for the planet but also contributes to perpetuating this inequality between men and women. the agricultural model of the future, and also for the cap, for example, is ecological and egalitarian. there, women are agents of change and play a key role in creating new rural jobs, such as in craft work or quality tourism. to do this, the european union has to lead this ecological and gender transition. we need the european and national institutions to support us, to support them. it's an opportunity for society as a whole.
in writing. i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs, marijana petir and lidia senra, on their good work together on a text which contains many of the requests which parliament has already expressed in its report on the future of the cap. a gender perspective is needed to combat the huge inequalities in access to land and agricultural property between men and women, as well as in the recognition of their status and rights as rural workers. the commission should take note of the serious deterioration in the situation of women in rural areas and integrate this gender perspective into the development of the cap. the report also points out that this will require improved implementation of rural policies, facilitating women's participation in decision-making.
