mr president, i have to say... i'm not sure. thank you, anna maria, rapporteur for this excellent report. thank you for your tireless work on behalf of children's rights. in these christmas days of lights, gifts, images of happy children, there is another face that is not bright but very dark and very cruel for millions of children who are sexually exploited in europe and in the world. the directive, which aims to combat sexual abuse and child pornography, is therefore the answer needed to ensure that children and adolescents who should be safe are not duped by adults who subject them to abuse, rape and abuse and then use those images, leading, in many cases, to suicide, because they are victims over and over again. it is necessary to criminalize sexual extortion, which affects more and more teenage girls every day. when will protection and increased protection for the most vulnerable victims be achieved? we need member states to have a clear definition of child pornography; tougher penalties for possession of child abuse material; to block websites that disseminate content; more police and judicial cooperation; and the internet industry to take responsibility for ensuring the safety of children once and for all. the difficulty of prosecuting these crossborder crimes makes it more difficult to fight them, but from this parliament we demand zero tolerance for those who violate the rights of children. so, prevent, prosecute, protect and respond to victims.
in writing. child abuse is a horrific crime, contrary to human dignity, and which must be prosecuted more effectively at european level especially in this age of digital opportunities and transnational crime. i am pleased to note that this report includes a balanced gender perspective: it recognises that sexual abuse impacts girls more, but also underlines that there is a significant percentage of boys involved. moreover, one recital acknowledges that 'men are less likely to report abuse'. i think we should go deeper into this pathway of making male victimization visible, imagining solutions to reduce social stigma and ways of intervention that are better adapted to the needs of children and boys who suffer abuse, from prevention to treatment. i would also like to draw attention to an important aspect of child sexual exploitation not covered in the report, which is not related to production but to consumption: the massive availability of pornography in this digital age and its negative impact on the moral and neuropsychological development of children, adolescents and adults. consumption is also a form of abuse. i would therefore encourage this matter to be placed more strongly on the future agenda of parliament.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president last year i was rapporteur for this report which mr marias is presenting today, and after a year the criticism we have is still mainly directed at the commission. we ask you once again to be more clear in your written and oral answers. you must also give us more information on the proceedings against the states, within the limits of the confidentiality you speak of. we must also be taken into account in the reform of the european citizens' initiative and we also demand that the commission once and for all enforce the precautionary principle, particularly in environmental matters and also in health. why not if this principle has not been established? because we continue to see in the committee how in many countries, including my own, in spain, projects are being torn apart and environmental impact studies are being torn apart, as well as access to information and citizen participation are being violated, as in the famous aarhus convention. i would also remind you that without this precautionary principle, other essential principles such as legal certainty or subsidiarity cannot be guaranteed, not to mention irreparable environmental damage. we must wait, as always, for disasters to happen and for the facts to be settled and then there is no solution? please apply the principle.
mr president, i have no doubt that the intention to reduce emissions in transport is sincere and shared by the majority of this house, but this is an unsustainable road map if we make the green transition dependent on the objective of reducing costs and increasing profits for private companies. it is environmentally unsustainable, according to the logic of the market, far from ecological sustainability, as we are seeing with the devastating expansion of biofuels or with the disproportionate growth of activities such as aviation. but it is also socially unsustainable, because consensus cannot be generated towards another production model through privatizations or the precariousness of working conditions. we must break with the strategy outlined in the white paper and reconcile social transition and ecological transition in the transport policies of the european union. this is the way forward in europe.
in writing. the emission reduction justified by the use of biofuels is a hoax. the current biofuel policy, even if limited to 7% use, will increase ghg emissions in the transport sector. if greenhouse gas emissions from indirect land use change are taken into account, biodiesel emissions are on average 80% higher than fossil diesel. although bioethanol has some reductions, it does not meet the minimum requirements required by the renewable energy directive. using land to grow raw materials for fuels is very energy-inefficient. while a football field planted with corn can fuel 2.4 cars for a year, the same expanse of photovoltaic panels could generate annual power for 260 cars. it should be added that, in the absence of sustainability criteria, the use of palm oil for biodiesel in europe has increased by 600%. the commission also found that the union industry had a significant market share in the union market, which was much higher than the union industry's market share. the sad conclusion is that european drivers are the biggest consumers of palm oil, without knowing it.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president the european union has recently concluded negotiations on a free trade and investment agreement with vietnam. an agreement that ignores the needs of the people without even having studied the impact it will have on human rights, already very deteriorated in that country. an agreement which, like ceta, further favours privileged transnational corporations by creating arbitration tribunals; an agreement which has no effective clauses on human rights; an agreement which only favours the interests of the past, especially by encouraging mining and the plundering of natural resources. with this agreement we shall have many more cases like the one we are dealing with today, mr van hoa, who, let us remember, was retaliated against for his peaceful resistance to the systematic violations by a company operating under the asean agreement. we are tired of the european union talking about human rights and then turning a blind eye, turning its back on its own principles, on human rights violations, always putting commercial interests first. we will never tire of demanding political consistency.
madam president, it is worrying what is happening in vietnam, where citizens have been imprisoned simply for wanting to express themselves and freely and democratically defend the human rights of their fellow citizens. many of those people imprisoned, moreover, are not without a fair trial, but have not been tried and there is no provision for trial for them. unfortunately, political and democratic abuses are taking place by the authorities of the communist and totalitarian regime in vietnam. that is why the european institutions must support and show solidarity with nguyen van hoa, who has been sentenced to seven years for informing the public about the abuses of the communist regime in vietnam. and the european institutions too, madam president, must condemn that asian country, vietnam, for its repressive policy and its tyrannical policy against its citizens.
author. madam president we are here to demand the freedom of teodora del carmen vásquez, evelyn beatriz hernández and all the women imprisoned in el salvador for having abortions or for suffering involuntary abortions. also to demand the total decriminalization of abortion in this country, but also in other parts of the world where abortion is prohibited or only allowed under certain circumstances. denial of sexual and reproductive health and safe and legal termination of pregnancy constitute a form of violence against women and a serious violation of their rights and dignity. the so-called gender equality cannot be achieved without guaranteeing women's free choice over their bodies. we demand that the european union and its member states be and ensure that the right to access voluntary family planning and safe and legal abortion is recognised for all women, whether in el salvador, in europe or in any other country in the world.
author. madam president, in el salvador abortion is prohibited in all cases. all of them. including rape, of course. but he was also punished as we in europe punish murders, with penalties of up to thirty years in prison. because it's considered aggravated homicide, even miscarriage. evelyn hernandez is a young salvadoran woman who was raped. he claims his son was stillborn. and yet, she's sentenced to 30 years in prison. and so are seventeen other women in salvadoran prisons, including teodora del carmen vásquez, whose sentence has just been confirmed by the judge. we are facing an enormous injustice and it is a punishment against women in one of the most violent countries in the entire region. it's a punishment against the most vulnerable. it's a repeated, insistent punishment against the victims themselves. and it's a punishment for the whole country, because what it does is block its progress, its development and its evolution. and we're not just talking about a matter of freedom. the price of the prohibition and extreme criminalization of abortion is nothing more and nothing less than the life and health of women. i deeply regret that there is no will and no consensus in this house on what the united nations high commissioner has called for: the decriminalisation of abortion in all circumstances and the possibility of abortion in some cases, at least, as in el salvador.
madam president, i have to ask you. teodora del carmen is thirty-four years old and has been in prison for more than ten years. ten years in prison for losing his daughter in premature birth, and the salvadoran authorities yesterday confirmed the thirty-year sentence. women in el salvador are criminalized. it's not just teodora. there are more than 30 cases of women who have suffered miscarriages and are in prisons deprived of their liberty. we cannot allow europe to allow women to be deprived of their freedom to decide their own lives in any part of the world. we must be aware that we are talking about human rights, and the european union's foreign and cooperation policy must guarantee the sexual and reproductive health rights of all women in the world. because their fight is our fight. our body is freedom. we will continue to work from europe for all women in the rest of the world.
madam president, since 1998 abortion has been persecuted. since the year 2000 almost more than 120 women have been prosecuted for this issue. sentenced to between 30 and 50 years. it doesn't matter if they were raped, it doesn't matter if their lives were in danger. today my thoughts go to teodora, who has already served ten years in prison; to evelyn, 18, who is facing more than thirty years in prison. and i think it is very important that this parliament should call for his release today and that the necessary legislative changes should be made to put an end to this situation. and i want to say that we are not far from it, because right now there are in the salvadoran congress initiatives to change the law. and that is why i think it is essential that the european union gives a push to these legislative changes so that we can change this situation. the european union delegation in el salvador is doing a good job in this regard and it is very important that, in view of what will happen next year with the elections in the country, this can be a real change that is operated and that these women can get out of prison and that, once and for all, a woman is never prosecuted again for having had an abortion.
mr president, in the european union the transport sector accounts for a third of energy consumption and a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions. it is also one of the sectors that has seen the greatest increase in emissions since 1990. therefore, moving towards a sustainable mobility model is a fundamental task. but again, we have to be careful with greenwashing. with those who use the fight against climate change to wash their image. the use of the misnamed natural gas and some biofuels is not an appropriate solution at all. these fuels only perpetuate the extractivist model and anchor us to a global model with excessive need or dependence on transport. we must therefore massively develop public transport and improve rail transport, improve intermodality and digitalisation in the sector and include externalities with the 'polluter pays' principle. these tools are some of the measures needed to help us breathe less polluted air.
